solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rates ski resort as "one star"

indicators.note: to resort is to sort again, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A grumpy critic gives a skiing resort a single-star review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as a holiday place but is the anagram signal: re-sort the letters of RATES SKI.
explanation.definitionFit: A single star symbol printed in text is called by this name, from the Greek for little star.

clue.text: Basic security for sailors

parts.note: security reads as safety arrangements, but it is the heavy object that keeps a ship secure at the sea bottom

explanation.definitionFit: A heavy hooked weight dropped to the seabed to hold a vessel in place, its fundamental security.

clue.text: Actor gives reading at new play

indicators.note: a new play of the letters, a rearrangement of reading at

explanation.surface: An actor gives a read-through of a freshly written drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new play' looks like the drama being read; it signals rearranging READING AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage performer who specialises in serious dramatic roles, a kind of actor.

clue.text: Has an inclination for debauched men

definitions.meaning: a stage or ship's mast that slopes is said to do this

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb meaning slopes at an angle and a plural noun for libertines.

clue.text: He will run away when things warm up

definitions.text: He will run away when things warm up

parts.words: He will run away when things warm up
parts.note: run away suggests fleeing, but the figure built of frozen flakes literally runs as it melts

explanation.definitionFit: A figure built of packed snow melts and runs as water when the weather gets warmer.

clue.text: Some British submarines return to spring a trap

indicators.note: return means that run is read backwards
some of the words means a run of letters is taken from inside British submarines

explanation.surface: A British submarine flotilla heads home in order to launch a surprise attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks HSUBMA out of BritiSH SUBMArines; 'return' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in wait and attacking by surprise is exactly to spring a trap on someone, used as a verb.

clue.text: Clue is "man" perhaps; answer is "male"

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of clue is and man might be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A setter explains a clue: one word given, a related word expected as the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pretends to be a crossword clue and its answer; 'perhaps' signals rearranging CLUE IS MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Of or relating to men, a direct synonym for male.

clue.text: States how old one is — it's the custom

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States
your age is how old you are

explanation.surface: A form asks for your age, which is simply the normal practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Customary practice or habit, especially in the way language is used, means the same as custom.

clue.text: It may be played on the lawn in summer

definitions.text: It may be played on the lawn in summer

parts.words: It may be played on the lawn in summer
parts.note: played suggests a garden game, but water is played on the grass from this rubber tube

explanation.definitionFit: A flexible tube for watering, whose jet a gardener directs over grass in dry weather.

clue.text: He's crazy — taking two banned substances

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine, an illegal drug
pot is slang for cannabis, also illegal

explanation.surface: A man's behaviour is put down to taking a couple of illegal drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, it describes a wild or eccentric idea or person, a near synonym.

clue.text: Awards no marks

parts.note: no, as zero or nil, is the letter O
scars are marks left on the skin

explanation.surface: A competition hands out prizes but gives no scores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no marks' looks like a verdict of zero points, but the words split into O and SCARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Film industry prizes are popularly called by this name, an example of awards.

clue.text: Fish deep in the sound

definitions.meaning: a perch-like food fish of sea and river
low in pitch, like the lowest voice or instrument

explanation.definitionFit: Spelt the same, one word names a fish and the other the lowest musical register.

clue.text: Roves around making deliveries

indicators.note: around means the letters of roves are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wanders about the place delivering parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls, each called a delivery, bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket term: each set of six balls bowled is one of these, so they are groups of deliveries.

clue.text: Fulfil expectations and take dimensions

definitions.meaning: to be good enough for what was hoped
to find the length and size of something, as a tailor might

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to prove adequate and, literally, to take sizes upward.

clue.text: One or two similar containers?

parts.note: the metal container is one object, yet its name is two words, each another word for such a container

explanation.definitionFit: A food storage vessel made of metal, named by a pair of words that each mean that vessel.

clue.text: Drug addict should stop behaving like that!

definitions.text: Drug addict should stop behaving like that!

parts.words: Drug addict should stop behaving like that!
parts.note: the phrase both tells an addict to quit a drug and, as an everyday retort, means stop talking nonsense

explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of disbelief telling someone to stop pretending, and also a literal call to quit drugs.

clue.text: The rest of the foot in the cavalry

definitions.text: The rest of the foot in the cavalry

parts.words: The rest of the foot in the cavalry
parts.note: foot looks like the foot soldiers, the infantry, but it is a rider's actual foot, resting in its loop

explanation.surface: A remark about what is left of the infantry within a mounted regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the foot' suggests infantry, as opposed to cavalry; read literally, it is a horseman's foot and its rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal loop hanging from a saddle in which a rider places a foot for support.

clue.text: Phone about disruption of trade causing delay

indicators.note: about means the call word goes around the rest

parts.note: to ring is to phone

indicators.note: disruption means the letters of trade are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A phone call about a breakdown in commerce explains the hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disruption' reads like a strike in the trade, but it is the anagram signal working on the word trade, and 'about' wraps the phone call round the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Slowing something down or holding it back is the action of causing delay.

clue.text: Can count on union uprising about tea break

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, a British trade union

indicators.note: uprising, in a down clue, means the word about is read upward, backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: break means the letters of tea are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: A workers' union rises up in a dispute over the tea break, relying on numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns RE into ER; 'break' makes ATE from TEA. The NUM is the British miners' union.
explanation.definitionFit: Being competent with numbers and arithmetic means being able to count.

clue.text: Anonymous nun made to change order

indicators.note: the letters of nun made change their order, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A nun is moved to a different religious order, without anyone giving her name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' suggests a religious order to go with the nun; it is the order of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no name given is a synonym for being nameless or anonymous.

clue.text: Expensive address

definitions.meaning: a way of addressing someone, as at the start of a letter

explanation.definitionFit: One word means costly and is also the greeting that opens a letter.

clue.text: Many take breaks at the summits

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, so many
rests are breaks or pauses

explanation.surface: Lots of climbers stop for a break when they reach the tops of the mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: The tops of hills or ridges are their highest points, synonyms for summits.

clue.text: Depreciate each novel writer

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of each are put in a new order

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Each new novel a writer produces lowers their standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but signals rearranging EACH into CHEA.
explanation.definitionFit: To lower the value or price of something is to depreciate it.

clue.text: Certainly in on the act

parts.note: a deed is an act

explanation.surface: Someone is surely in on the scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: An emphatic adverb of agreement, meaning certainly or truly.

clue.text: Possibly able to speak with added detail

indicators.note: possibly signals that able may be rearranged into another arrangement

parts.note: to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: A speaker who may well be able to talk at length, filling in every particular.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worked out in full, with many intricate parts, has had detail added.

clue.text: Maurice has a heart of gold

indicators.note: the heart of the name is everything inside its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A man named Maurice is kind-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of gold' is the idiom for kindness; split, it gives the selection and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare adjective from the Latin for gold, meaning containing or relating to that metal.

clue.text: Protection, with strings attached

parts.note: with strings attached normally means with conditions, but here the protective garment is literally tied on with strings

explanation.definitionFit: A cook's garment guards clothes from splashes and is tied at the back with ties.

clue.text: A period return for Wembley, say

indicators.note: return means the words are read backwards

parts.note: an is a form of the indefinite article a
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A football fan buys a return ticket to Wembley for the season.
explanation.walkthrough: Wembley is England's national football stadium in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A large stadium for sport or shows; Wembley is an example.

clue.text: Undirected commercial break

parts.note: an ad is a television commercial
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: An unplanned advertising break with no one in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat floating without control, or a person without aim, is without direction.

clue.text: A pupil originally with little desire to take courses

indicators.note: originally means only the first letter of pupil is taken

parts.note: petite means small or little

explanation.surface: A small schoolchild who was at first not keen on enrolling for classes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'courses' suggests school courses to match the pupil; they are the courses of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hunger is a wish to eat, here to work through the courses of a meal.

clue.text: Former name to cause a stir

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
to cite is to name or mention

explanation.surface: Naming an ex-partner is bound to stir up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse feelings or agitate is to stir things up, a close synonym.

clue.text: Big end about to be made bigger

indicators.note: about means the word end is placed around the other piece

parts.note: large means big

explanation.surface: The large end of something is due to be expanded even further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big end' reads as the engine part; split, 'Big' is the word inserted and 'end' the one placed about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Increased in size, a past participle meaning expanded or grown larger.
